title: What is voice therapy?
intro: Voice therapy is a treatment that helps people with voice problems, such as hoarseness, strain, weak voice or loss of voice. A speech and language therapist teaches exercises and healthy habits. It is used for many causes, including overuse, nodules, nerve problems and gender-related voice change.

sections.heading: Why voice problems occur
paragraphs: Voices can be affected by overuse or misuse, such as shouting or talking for long periods, by infections, reflux, smoking, dryness, nodules or polyps on the vocal folds, nerve damage, neurological disease or emotional stress. Hoarseness lasting more than three to four weeks should be checked by a doctor, especially in smokers.

sections.heading: Assessment
paragraphs: A doctor, usually an ear, nose and throat specialist, looks at the vocal folds with a camera. The therapist listens to the voice, measures how long you can hold a sound, and asks about habits, work and medicines. Together they set goals, such as clearer voice, less strain or greater endurance.

sections.heading: What therapy involves
paragraphs: Therapy includes breathing training, relaxation of neck and shoulder muscles, exercises for resonance, pitch and loudness, and techniques such as semi-occluded vocal tract exercises, for example humming or talking through a straw. You learn to use the voice efficiently and to avoid habits that cause harm. Sessions are weekly, with daily home practice.

sections.heading: Voice care
paragraphs: Drink enough water, avoid smoking and irritants, treat reflux, avoid whispering and clearing the throat too often, rest the voice after heavy use and use amplification in noisy places. Teachers, singers and call-centre staff are particularly at risk. Voice therapy can also help transgender people to adjust pitch and resonance.

sections.heading: Outcomes
paragraphs: Many people improve within weeks to months. Some conditions, such as nodules, may disappear with therapy, while others also need medicines or surgery. Consistent practice is key. Contact your doctor if there is no progress or if symptoms get worse.

examples.title: Practising daily
examples.text: Imagine you have strained your voice at work. You could do your humming exercises daily and rest the voice during breaks.

examples.title: Seeking examination
examples.text: Suppose you have been hoarse for six weeks. You might ask for an ear, nose and throat check.
